main_text.p: periem,formæ,aut totius substantiæ corru-ptelam.Rationes autem,quibus ad hæc no-ua,inauditaq; morborum genera similaris partis statuenda fuerit adductus,propone-re nos haud pigebit. Prima harum,hæc est. Quæ partes (inquit) similares appellantur« tria hæc in se discreta continent,materiam,« temperamentum,& essentiam,quę illarum« species dici consueuit.Hæc ille,quibus af-«sentiri[?] non possumus, quando ambiguita-te,& dubio non carere uidentur.Primum ma-teria,forma & temperamentum,quibus mi-stum corpus constat,a se discreta esse, & con-sistere nequeunt,tantisper dum uiuit ipsum corpus.Non enim discerni possunt,nisi corru-ptione & morte: quandoquidem naturalis corporis essentiales partes sunt materia & forma,sine quibus nulla corporea substan-tia subsistere potest. Etenim corpus natu-rale constituunt. His adde quód nulla ma-teria per se,& sine aliqua forma in rerum na-tura subsistit,quoniam non est ens actu,sed potentia.Tantisper igitur uiuunt nostri cor-poris partes similares,quales sunt os,ner-uus,ligamentum,tendo,membrana,& aliæ similes, dum materia & forma constant.Hæc igitur prima Fernelij ratio claudicat, nec

page.notes: The quotation marks « in the right margin (lines 6 to 9) are printed marks, transcribed as notes at their places. Line 1 opens with a fragment ("periem,") and stays one. Line 9, "sentiri", is doubtful: the first letter looks like a long s or l, so it is marked [?]. Printed spellings such as "quód", "quę" and "Fernelij" are kept as they stand. The running head is set in spaced capitals, read as CAVSAS, PROGYMNASMATA.
